set1.io: Describe laboratory findings associated with platelet abnormalities
set1.q: A 52-year-old man has a low automated platelet count. His smear shows platelet clumps and platelets surrounding neutrophils. What does this indicate?
opts: A falsely low count
Correct. Clumping and platelets ringing neutrophils (satellitism) make the automated count read falsely low, which is spurious thrombocytopenia.
Disseminated intravascular coagulation
Disseminated intravascular coagulation shows a low count with prolonged clotting times, low fibrinogen and a high D-dimer, not clumping on the smear.
Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura shows fragmented red cells (schistocytes) on the smear, not platelet clumps.
Immune thrombocytopenia
A true immune thrombocytopenia has few platelets on the smear. Clumping means the platelets are present but miscounted.

set1.io: Define: hemostasis, primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, thrombus, fibrinolysis, fibrin degradation products, D-dimer
set1.q: A 44-year-old woman is taught the three overlapping stages of hemostasis. Which set is correct?
opts: Primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, thrombosis
Thrombosis is a pathologic clot forming in a vessel, not a stage of normal hemostasis. The third stage is fibrinolysis, the breakdown of the clot.
Platelet plug, fibrin clot, embolism
An embolism is a clot that has moved somewhere. The third stage of hemostasis is the dissolving of the clot by fibrinolysis.
Primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, fibrinolysis

Correct. Hemostasis has three overlapping stages: the platelet plug (primary hemostasis), the fibrin clot built by the coagulation factors (secondary hemostasis) and the breakdown of the clot (fibrinolysis).
Coagulation, thrombosis, embolism
These describe clot behavior in disease. Normal hemostasis runs from platelet plug, through coagulation, to fibrinolysis.

set1.io: Discuss diagnostic testing for: primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, fibrinolysis
set1.q: A 50-year-old man has a positive fibrin monomer test. What activity does a positive result indicate?
opts: Platelet aggregation
Platelet aggregation is assessed by function tests such as light transmission aggregometry. Fibrin monomers reflect thrombin acting on fibrinogen.
Thrombin activity

Correct. A positive fibrin monomer test is indicative of thrombin activity and is consistent with intravascular coagulation; severe liver disease and inflammatory disorders can also give a positive result.
Vitamin K deficiency
Vitamin K deficiency prolongs the prothrombin time by lowering vitamin K dependent factors. It is not what a fibrin monomer test detects.
Complete absence of fibrinogen
Afibrinogenemia would leave no substrate for thrombin to act on. Fibrin monomers form when thrombin cleaves fibrinogen.

set1.io: Describe laboratory findings associated with platelet abnormalities
set1.q: A 65-year-old man with uremia bleeds easily. His platelet count, prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time are normal. Which category fits?
opts: Platelet dysfunction
Correct. Normal prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time with bleeding suggest platelet dysfunction; uremia is one cause, and platelet function testing is abnormal.
Factor VII deficiency
Factor VII deficiency prolongs the prothrombin time, which is normal here.
Hemophilia A
Hemophilia A prolongs the partial thromboplastin time, which is normal here.
Hypofibrinogenemia
Low fibrinogen prolongs the prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time, and both are normal here.

set1.io: Compare and contrast laboratory studies used to evaluate bleeding and thrombotic disorders
set1.q: A 36-year-old woman has easy bruising and bleeding gums. Which initial set of studies is appropriate?
opts: Prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time and D-dimer
That is the thrombotic workup. A bleeding patient needs the platelet count and smear and fibrinogen instead of D-dimer.
Blood count with smear, clotting times and fibrinogen
Correct. The bleeding workup is a blood count with differential and peripheral smear, prothrombin time with international normalized ratio, activated partial thromboplastin time and fibrinogen.
D-dimer and fibrin monomers only
These markers of clot formation and breakdown do not screen platelets or coagulation factors.
Bleeding time alone
One test cannot screen every cause of bleeding, and platelets, factors and fibrinogen all need evaluating.

set1.io: Discuss diagnostic testing for: primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, fibrinolysis
set1.q: A 12-year-old boy has a prolonged partial thromboplastin time that corrects when mixed one to one with normal plasma. What does this suggest?
opts: An inhibitor
An inhibitor also blocks the factors in the normal plasma, so the prolonged time persists after mixing.
A factor deficiency
Correct. Correction on a mixing study suggests a factor deficiency, because normal plasma supplies the missing factor.
Lupus anticoagulant
Lupus anticoagulant is an inhibitor, so the prolonged time does not correct with normal plasma.
A platelet disorder
Platelet disorders give a normal partial thromboplastin time, so a mixing study is not used for them.

set1.io: Describe laboratory findings associated with platelet abnormalities
set1.q: A 44-year-old man has a platelet count of 80,000 per microliter (adult reference 140,000 to 400,000). Which term applies?
opts: Thrombocytosis
Thrombocytosis is a platelet count that is too high, above the reference range. This count is well below the lower limit instead.
A normal count
The adult reference range is 140,000 to 400,000 per microliter, and 80,000 falls below it.
Pseudothrombocytosis
This count is low, not falsely high. A spurious low count is instead pseudothrombocytopenia, caused by platelet clumping.
Thrombocytopenia
Correct. A platelet count well below the lower reference limit is thrombocytopenia, here a count under even the 100,000 per microliter figure used to define it.

set1.io: Discuss diagnostic testing for: primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, fibrinolysis
set1.q: A 30-year-old man undergoes a bedside bleeding time (reference 3 to 10 minutes). At which platelet count is the result meaningful?
opts: Above 100,000 per microliter
Correct. Bleeding time is only useful if the platelet count is above 100,000 per microliter, because thrombocytopenia itself lengthens bleeding time.
Below 50,000 per microliter
Below this level thrombocytopenia already causes prolonged bleeding, so the test cannot isolate a platelet function problem.
Below 20,000 per microliter
At this count spontaneous bleeding and petechiae are expected from the low number alone, which makes bleeding time uninterpretable.
Below 10,000 per microliter
At this count the concern is spontaneous intracranial bleeding. Bleeding time cannot be interpreted with so few platelets.

set1.io: Describe laboratory findings associated with platelet abnormalities
set1.q: A 27-year-old man has a normal platelet count and a bleeding time of 18 minutes (reference 3 to 10). What does this suggest?
opts: Coagulation factors are deficient
Factor deficiencies prolong the prothrombin time or partial thromboplastin time, not bleeding time as the primary finding.
Fibrinolysis is excessive
Excess fibrinolysis is assessed by other tests, such as euglobulin clot lysis time. Bleeding time reflects the platelet plug.
Platelets are not working well
Correct. With a normal platelet count a prolonged bleeding time signals a platelet function problem, a primary hemostasis defect.
The platelet count is falsely high
The count is normal, and a falsely high count would not lengthen the bleeding time.

set1.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set1.q: A 49-year-old man not on warfarin has an international normalized ratio of 2.6 (reference 0.8 to 1.2). Which cause fits?
opts: Immune thrombocytopenia
Immune thrombocytopenia lowers the platelet count and leaves the prothrombin time normal.
Liver disease
Correct. Off warfarin, an abnormal prothrombin time or international normalized ratio may indicate a bleeding disorder, a clotting disorder, liver disease or vitamin K deficiency.
Hemophilia A
Hemophilia A prolongs the partial thromboplastin time and leaves the prothrombin time normal.
Acute thrombosis
Acute thrombosis typically shows a raised D-dimer with a normal prothrombin time.

set1.io: Describe laboratory findings associated with platelet abnormalities
set1.q: A 19-year-old woman has heavy menses and easy bruising. Which inherited bleeding disorder is the most common overall?
opts: Hemophilia A
Hemophilia A, factor VIII deficiency, is common among the factor deficiencies, but von Willebrand disease is the most common inherited bleeding disorder overall.
von Willebrand disease
Correct. von Willebrand disease is the most common inherited bleeding disorder, and it is tested with von Willebrand factor antigen, activity and a factor VIII level.
Hemophilia B
Hemophilia B, factor IX deficiency, is less common than von Willebrand disease.
Factor XIII deficiency
Factor XIII deficiency is rare, marked by umbilical stump bleeding and lifelong severe bleeding, and far less common than von Willebrand disease.

set1.io: Describe laboratory findings associated with platelet abnormalities
set1.q: A 70-year-old man bleeds, and a physician reviews platelet counts. Which statement about count and bleeding is correct?
opts: Only low counts cause bleeding
Extreme thrombocythemia can also cause bleeding, so a very high count does not protect against it.
Only high counts cause bleeding
Thrombocytopenia clearly causes bleeding, with risk rising as the count falls.
Counts never cause bleeding with a normal prothrombin time
A normal prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time with bleeding actually points toward a platelet problem, quantitative or qualitative.
Very low and very high counts can both cause bleeding
Correct. Thrombocytopenia and extreme thrombocythemia, above 1,000 times 10 to the ninth per liter, can both cause bleeding.

set1.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set1.q: A 59-year-old man with severe malabsorption has a prolonged prothrombin time. Which liver-made protein, dependent on vitamin K, explains this?
opts: Fibrin
Fibrin is the clot formed from fibrinogen. It is not the vitamin K dependent liver protein behind this result.
Prothrombin
Correct. Prothrombin is produced by the liver and depends on vitamin K intake and absorption, so vitamin K deficiency prolongs the prothrombin time.
Plasmin
Plasmin degrades fibrin and is not the protein whose production depends on vitamin K.
von Willebrand factor
von Willebrand factor tethers platelets in primary hemostasis. It is not the vitamin K dependent protein that the prothrombin time depends on.

set1.io: Discuss diagnostic testing for: primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, fibrinolysis
set1.q: A 55-year-old man has a prothrombin time ordered. Which pathways does it assess?
opts: The intrinsic and common pathways
That describes the activated partial thromboplastin time, which uses a phospholipid activator to assess the intrinsic pathway plus the common pathway.
Platelet adhesion and aggregation
Platelet plug formation is primary hemostasis and is tested by counts and platelet function studies, not the prothrombin time.
The extrinsic and common pathways
Correct. The prothrombin time measures fibrin clot formation after tissue factor is added, so it reflects the extrinsic pathway plus the common pathway factors.
Breakdown of fibrin by plasmin
Fibrinolysis is evaluated by tests such as D-dimer. The prothrombin time measures clot formation.

set1.io: Describe laboratory findings associated with platelet abnormalities
set1.q: A 22-year-old woman has thrombocytopenia, and her smear shows large, pale gray platelets. Which syndrome fits?
opts: Gray platelet syndrome
Correct. Macrothrombocytopenia with gray platelets on the smear is gray platelet syndrome.
May-Hegglin anomaly
May-Hegglin anomaly (a myosin heavy chain 9 disorder) shows inclusions within neutrophils, not gray platelets.
Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura shows fragmented red cells (schistocytes), not gray platelets.
Spurious thrombocytopenia
Spurious thrombocytopenia shows platelet clumps and satellitism, not large gray platelets.

set1.io: Discuss indications for ordering coagulation studies
set1.q: A 45-year-old man with cirrhosis has easy bruising. Which initial test evaluates his secondary hemostasis?
opts: D-dimer alone
D-dimer marks fibrin breakdown and is not a screen for reduced clotting factor synthesis.
Bleeding time alone
Bleeding time tests the platelet plug, which does not reflect how well the liver makes clotting factors.
Prothrombin time with international normalized ratio
Correct. Liver disease is an indication for coagulation studies; the liver makes prothrombin, so the prothrombin time and international normalized ratio assess it.
Platelet aggregation alone
Platelet aggregation tests platelet function and would not reveal low coagulation factors from liver disease.

set1.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set1.q: A 58-year-old man has a prolonged prothrombin time with a low platelet count. Why can one abnormal value not diagnose disseminated intravascular coagulation?
opts: Other conditions can cause each abnormality
Correct. Each abnormality has other causes, for example liver failure, vitamin K deficiency and major blood loss, so the overall picture matters.
The prothrombin time is always normal in it
The prothrombin time is prolonged in disseminated intravascular coagulation, not normal.
Platelet counts rise in it
The platelet count falls in it, because platelets are consumed in clots throughout the body.
Only a bleeding time can diagnose it
Bleeding time is not a diagnostic test for it, and the diagnosis rests on the pattern of the platelet count, clotting times, fibrin degradation products and inhibitors.

set1.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set1.q: A 62-year-old woman has normal prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time, fibrinogen and platelets, and a raised D-dimer. Which interpretation fits?
opts: Acute thrombosis
Correct. A raised D-dimer with normal coagulation studies and platelets is the acute thrombosis pattern, and D-dimer is nonspecific.
Disseminated intravascular coagulation
Disseminated intravascular coagulation would also prolong the clotting times and lower fibrinogen and platelets.
Hemophilia A
Hemophilia A prolongs the partial thromboplastin time, which is normal here.
Platelet dysfunction
Platelet dysfunction does not raise D-dimer and is not reflected by the coagulation screens.

set1.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set1.q: A 50-year-old man with sepsis has a prolonged prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time, low fibrinogen, a raised D-dimer and a low platelet count. Which diagnosis fits?
opts: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura lowers the platelet count but leaves the prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time and fibrinogen normal.
Immune thrombocytopenia
Immune thrombocytopenia lowers only the platelet count, with normal clotting times and fibrinogen.
Disseminated intravascular coagulation
Correct. This is the pattern of acute disseminated intravascular coagulation: prolonged screens, low fibrinogen and platelets, and a raised D-dimer.
Vitamin K antagonist effect
A vitamin K antagonist prolongs the prothrombin time alone, with a normal partial thromboplastin time, fibrinogen and platelet count.

set1.io: Discuss diagnostic testing for: primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, fibrinolysis
set1.q: A 62-year-old man has a negative fibrin monomer test. What does this result mean?
opts: Intravascular coagulation is excluded
A negative test does not exclude intravascular coagulation. A negative result can occur even when intravascular coagulation is present.
Plasmin activity is absent
Fibrin monomers reflect thrombin activity, not plasmin. A negative result says nothing definite about plasmin.
The fibrinogen level is normal
Fibrinogen is measured on its own assay, such as the Clauss method. A fibrin monomer test does not report its level.
Intravascular coagulation is not excluded
Correct. A negative fibrin monomer test does not mean intravascular coagulation is absent; a positive one indicates thrombin activity.

set1.io: Discuss diagnostic testing for: primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, fibrinolysis
set1.q: A 57-year-old man has a fibrinogen of 8.2 grams per liter (reference 2.0 to 4.0). Which risk is increased?
opts: Hemorrhage after traumatic surgery
That risk applies to a very low fibrinogen, below 0.5 grams per liter, not a high one.
Hemophilia
Hemophilia is a clotting factor deficiency, not something a high fibrinogen indicates.
Platelet dysfunction
Platelet function is tested separately. A high fibrinogen does not indicate a platelet problem.
Coronary and cerebrovascular disease
Correct. A fibrinogen above 7.0 grams per liter is a significant risk for both coronary artery and cerebrovascular disease.

set1.io: Compare and contrast laboratory studies used to evaluate bleeding and thrombotic disorders
set1.q: A 55-year-old man has a risk assessment for arterial thrombosis. Which two laboratory results are independent risk factors?
opts: Bleeding time and platelet count
These assess platelet plug formation and are not cited as independent risk factors for arterial thrombosis.
Mixing study and reptilase time
These are problem-solving tests for prolonged clotting times and not risk factors.
Mean platelet volume and fibrin monomers
Neither is identified as an independent risk factor for arterial thrombosis.
Prothrombin time and D-dimer
Correct. The prothrombin time and D-dimer are independent risk factors for arterial thrombosis.

set1.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set1.q: A 40-year-old man with no bleeding history has a prolonged partial thromboplastin time found before surgery, and a normal prothrombin time. Which deficiency fits?
opts: Factor VIII
Factor VIII deficiency, hemophilia A, prolongs the activated partial thromboplastin time but comes with a bleeding history.
Factor IX
Factor IX deficiency, hemophilia B, also causes bleeding, so a patient with no bleeding history is less likely to have it.
Factor XII
Correct. Factor XII deficiency prolongs the activated partial thromboplastin time but does not cause bleeding.
Factor XI
Factor XI deficiency comes with a bleeding history. Without one, factor XII deficiency or lupus anticoagulant fits better.

set1.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set1.q: A 27-year-old woman has a low platelet count with a normal prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time and platelet function analysis. Which diagnosis fits?
opts: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
Disseminated intravascular coagulation also has a low count but prolongs the prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time.
von Willebrand disease
von Willebrand disease has a normal platelet count and a prolonged partial thromboplastin time.
Early liver failure
Early liver failure prolongs the prothrombin time and leaves the platelet count normal.
Immune thrombocytopenia
Correct. Immune thrombocytopenia, thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, hemolytic uremic syndrome and heparin-induced thrombocytopenia all give a low count with normal clotting times.

set1.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set1.q: A 41-year-old man bleeds despite a normal platelet count, platelet function, prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time. Which deficiency should be considered?
opts: Hemophilia A
Hemophilia A prolongs the partial thromboplastin time, which is normal in this patient.
Factor VII deficiency
Factor VII deficiency prolongs the prothrombin time, which is normal in this patient.
Factor XIII deficiency

Correct. Factor XIII or alpha-2 antiplasmin deficiency fits: normal prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time with bleeding suggest a platelet disorder, mild von Willebrand disease, factor XIII or alpha-2 antiplasmin deficiency, or impaired fibrinolysis.
Heparin effect
Heparin prolongs the partial thromboplastin time and thrombin time.

set1.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set1.q: A 48-year-old woman has a D-dimer above the reference limit of 250 micrograms per liter. What does a positive result confirm?
opts: Thrombin and plasmin were both generated
Correct. D-dimer is produced only by plasmin acting on cross-linked fibrin, so its presence confirms that both thrombin generation and plasmin generation have occurred.
A deep vein thrombosis specifically
D-dimer is a nonspecific marker of fibrin breakdown. It is raised in acute thrombosis but also in disseminated intravascular coagulation, pregnancy and many acute illnesses.
Platelet dysfunction
Platelet function is tested by aggregometry or platelet function analysis. D-dimer reflects fibrin formation and breakdown instead.
A factor VIII deficiency
A factor VIII deficiency prolongs the activated partial thromboplastin time. It does not produce fibrin breakdown products.

set1.io: Discuss diagnostic testing for: primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, fibrinolysis
set1.q: A 60-year-old man on heparin has a prolonged thrombin time. Which test stays normal, pointing to heparin rather than a fibrinogen defect?
opts: Activated partial thromboplastin time
Heparin prolongs the activated partial thromboplastin time, so it does not stay normal.
Reptilase time
Correct. The reptilase time is normal with heparin because it mainly assesses fibrinogen function, separating heparin effect from a fibrinogen problem.
D-dimer
D-dimer marks fibrin breakdown and does not distinguish heparin from a fibrinogen defect.
Mean platelet volume
Mean platelet volume describes platelet size and plays no part in separating these causes.

set1.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set1.q: A 70-year-old man takes warfarin, and his international normalized ratio is 1.4 (goal 2.0 to 3.0). What is the concern?
opts: Clot risk
Correct. On warfarin a low international normalized ratio means too little anticoagulation and a risk of clotting.
Bleeding risk
A high international normalized ratio, above goal, signals bleeding risk. This value is below goal.
Platelet failure
The international normalized ratio comes from the prothrombin time and does not evaluate platelets.
Liver failure
Liver failure prolongs the prothrombin time and raises the international normalized ratio, so a low value is not the pattern.

set1.io: Discuss diagnostic testing for: primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, fibrinolysis
set1.q: A 57-year-old man takes aspirin and bruises easily. Which laboratory study directly evaluates platelet function?
opts: Prothrombin time
The prothrombin time assesses the extrinsic and common coagulation pathways, not platelets.
Light transmission aggregometry
Correct. Platelet function testing includes light transmission aggregometry, lumiaggregometry, the platelet function analyzer and flow cytometry.
Thrombin time
Thrombin time screens the fibrinogen-to-fibrin step. It does not test how platelets behave.
D-dimer
D-dimer marks fibrin breakdown and cannot show whether platelets aggregate normally.

set1.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set1.q: A 39-year-old man has an isolated prolonged partial thromboplastin time with low fibrinogen activity and a normal fibrinogen antigen. Which diagnosis fits?
opts: Hypofibrinogenemia
Hypofibrinogenemia has low antigen as well as low activity, because there is too little fibrinogen.
Lupus anticoagulant
Lupus anticoagulant is sought when fibrinogen is normal and the mix does not correct.
von Willebrand disease
von Willebrand disease is sought after a correcting mix with a low factor VIII, not from a fibrinogen pattern.
Dysfibrinogenemia
Correct. Low fibrinogen activity with normal antigen means the fibrinogen is present but does not work, which is dysfibrinogenemia.

set2.io: Describe laboratory findings associated with platelet abnormalities
set2.q: A 52-year-old woman has a platelet count of 15,000 per microliter (adult reference 140,000 to 400,000). Which finding is expected?
opts: Petechiae and spontaneous bleeding
Correct. Below 20,000 per microliter the patient may have spontaneous bleeding and petechiae.
Bleeding only after major surgery
Below 50,000 bleeding already occurs with mild or moderate trauma, and below 20,000 it becomes spontaneous.
Bruising without spontaneous bleeding
Bruising alone is the tier below 50,000 per microliter. By 20,000 spontaneous bleeding and petechiae appear.
Bleeding into joints and muscles
Hemarthrosis and deep muscle hematomas are features of clotting factor deficiency such as hemophilia, not of thrombocytopenia.

set2.io: Describe laboratory findings associated with platelet abnormalities
set2.q: A 33-year-old woman has thrombocytopenia, and her smear shows fragmented red blood cells. What are these fragments called?
opts: Schistocytes
Correct. The smear in thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura shows red cell fragments, called schistocytes, in addition to the thrombocytopenia.
Target cells
Target cells have a central dark spot and are not fragments. They are not the finding in thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura.
Spherocytes
Spherocytes are small dense round red cells that lack central pallor. Fragmented, helmet-shaped cells are schistocytes.
Teardrop cells
Teardrop cells have a single tapered tail. The fragmented cells of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura are schistocytes.

set2.io: Discuss diagnostic testing for: primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, fibrinolysis
set2.q: A 24-year-old woman has mucosal bleeding and a normal platelet count. Which studies evaluate von Willebrand disease?
opts: Prothrombin time and international normalized ratio
These screen the extrinsic pathway and are normal in von Willebrand disease. They do not test the factor.
von Willebrand antigen, activity and factor VIII
Correct. The von Willebrand studies are von Willebrand factor antigen and activity plus a factor VIII level.
D-dimer and fibrin monomers
These are markers of clot formation and breakdown, not a measure of von Willebrand factor.
Fibrinogen and thrombin time
These assess the final step of clot formation and are normal in von Willebrand disease. They do not measure the factor.

set2.io: Describe laboratory findings associated with platelet abnormalities
set2.q: A 54-year-old man with cirrhosis has an enlarged spleen and a low platelet count. Which mechanism lowers the circulating count?
opts: Consumption in clots
Consumption is the mechanism of disseminated intravascular coagulation, in which platelets are used up in clots throughout the body.
Sequestration in the spleen
Correct. Hypersplenism pools platelets in an enlarged spleen, so fewer circulate. Increased platelet sequestration is a cause of thrombocytopenia.
Impaired marrow production
Impaired production arises from deficiency, chemotherapy or marrow failure. In hypersplenism the marrow is making platelets that are pooled.
Immune destruction
Immune destruction involves antibodies against platelets. Hypersplenism pools normal platelets in the enlarged spleen.

set2.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set2.q: A newborn has umbilical stump bleeding and lifelong severe bleeding later. The prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time and thrombin time are normal. Which deficiency fits?
opts: Factor VII
Factor VII deficiency prolongs the prothrombin time, which is normal in this patient.
Factor XIII
Correct. Factor XIII deficiency gives umbilical stump bleeding and lifelong severe bleeding of any tissue with normal screening tests.
Factor VIII
Factor VIII deficiency prolongs the partial thromboplastin time.
Factor IX
Factor IX deficiency also prolongs the partial thromboplastin time.

set2.io: Define: hemostasis, primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, thrombus, fibrinolysis, fibrin degradation products, D-dimer
set2.q: A 22-year-old woman has von Willebrand disease. Which phase of hemostasis does the missing factor serve?
opts: Primary hemostasis
Correct. von Willebrand factor tethers platelets to exposed subendothelial collagen, so its deficiency impairs formation of the platelet plug.
Secondary hemostasis
Secondary hemostasis is the coagulation cascade that makes cross-linked fibrin. von Willebrand factor acts earlier, at the platelet plug.
Fibrinolysis
Fibrinolysis is the plasmin-mediated breakdown of a clot. von Willebrand factor helps platelets stick, which comes first.
Vasoconstriction
Vasoconstriction narrows the injured vessel and is a separate component of hemostasis. von Willebrand factor tethers platelets to collagen.

set2.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set2.q: A 33-year-old woman has calf cramping and a low suspicion of thrombosis. In which situation does a D-dimer add the most value?
opts: When a normal result is expected
Correct. D-dimer is most useful for its negative predictive value: a normal result helps exclude thrombosis, so it adds value only when a normal result is plausible.
When a clot is already known to be present
A raised D-dimer is expected when a clot is known to exist, so it adds no new information.
When the clot location is needed
D-dimer is nonspecific and does not show where a clot is. Imaging locates it.
When platelet function is in doubt
Platelet function is evaluated by aggregometry or platelet function analysis, not D-dimer.

set2.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set2.q: A 66-year-old woman takes warfarin, and her international normalized ratio is 4.8 (goal 2.0 to 3.0). What is the concern?
opts: Clot risk
A low international normalized ratio on warfarin signals clot risk. This value is above goal.
Platelet excess
The international normalized ratio standardizes the prothrombin time and does not assess platelet number.
Fibrinolysis
Fibrinolysis is evaluated by D-dimer, not the international normalized ratio.
Bleeding risk
Correct. On warfarin a high international normalized ratio means over-anticoagulation and a risk of bleeding.

set2.io: Discuss diagnostic testing for: primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, fibrinolysis
set2.q: A 38-year-old woman has thrombocytopenia. Which platelet index describes the uniformity of platelet size and helps with the differential diagnosis?
opts: Mean corpuscular volume
Mean corpuscular volume reports the size of red blood cells, not platelets.
Red cell distribution width
Red cell distribution width measures variation in red cell size. It says nothing about platelet size.
Mean platelet volume
Correct. Mean platelet volume indicates the uniformity of size of the platelet population and is used for the differential diagnosis of thrombocytopenia.
Bleeding time
Bleeding time measures how long a standardized skin puncture bleeds. It reflects platelet function but not platelet size.

set2.io: Discuss diagnostic testing for: primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, fibrinolysis
set2.q: A 43-year-old woman needs a fibrinogen level measured. Which method is preferred?
opts: A prothrombin time derived value
A fibrinogen estimated from the prothrombin time is the less-preferred method.
Bleeding time
Bleeding time tests platelet plug formation, not fibrinogen.
Mean platelet volume
Mean platelet volume describes platelet size, not fibrinogen.
The Clauss assay
Correct. The Clauss assay is preferred over a prothrombin time derived fibrinogen.

set2.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set2.q: A 35-year-old woman has a low suspicion of thrombosis, and her D-dimer is below the reference limit. What does the normal result do?
opts: It confirms thrombosis
A raised D-dimer is nonspecific, so it cannot confirm thrombosis, and a normal value does the opposite, helping to exclude it.
It shows the clotting factors are normal
Factor activity is judged by prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time. D-dimer only reflects fibrin breakdown.
It measures platelet function
D-dimer measures fibrin breakdown, not platelet behavior. Platelet function has its own tests, such as aggregometry.
It helps exclude thrombosis
Correct. D-dimer is best used for its high negative predictive value: a normal result helps exclude thrombosis.

set2.io: Discuss indications for ordering coagulation studies
set2.q: A 37-year-old woman bleeds easily, and her prothrombin time and international normalized ratio are normal. What does this mean?
opts: A coagulopathy is not excluded
Correct. A normal prothrombin time and international normalized ratio do not rule out coagulopathy; platelet disorders and other defects can coexist.
A coagulopathy is excluded
A normal prothrombin time does not exclude a coagulopathy, because it tests only part of the system.
Platelet function is normal
The prothrombin time does not assess platelets. Platelet dysfunction with bleeding gives normal prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time.
Fibrinolysis is normal
Fibrinolysis is evaluated by breakdown-product tests, such as D-dimer, not the prothrombin time.

set2.io: Describe laboratory findings associated with platelet abnormalities
set2.q: A 61-year-old man has a platelet count of 6,000 per microliter (adult reference 140,000 to 400,000). Which risk is highest?
opts: Bruising only with major trauma
Bruising easily starts below 50,000 per microliter. At 6,000 the risk is far greater than bruising with major trauma.
Excess bleeding only with surgery
At this count bleeding is spontaneous, and surgery is not needed to provoke it.
Spontaneous intracranial bleeding
Correct. Below 10,000 per microliter the patient is at risk for spontaneous intracranial bleeding and serious hemorrhage.
No added risk until the count is lower still
Below 10,000 per microliter is already the highest-risk tier, with risk of spontaneous intracranial bleeding.

set2.io: Discuss indications for ordering coagulation studies
set2.q: A 68-year-old man takes warfarin for atrial fibrillation. Which laboratory test monitors the therapy?
opts: D-dimer
D-dimer helps rule out thrombosis. It is not used to adjust warfarin.
Platelet count
The platelet count evaluates primary hemostasis, which warfarin does not act on.
International normalized ratio
Correct. Warfarin monitoring is an indication for coagulation studies, and the international normalized ratio is the test used, with a typical goal of 2.0 to 3.0.
Bleeding time
Bleeding time tests platelet plug formation, not the vitamin K dependent factors that warfarin reduces.

set2.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set2.q: A 35-year-old woman has a prothrombin time of 19 seconds (reference 11 to 13) and a normal activated partial thromboplastin time. Which deficiency fits?
opts: Factor VII
Correct. An isolated prolonged prothrombin time points to the extrinsic pathway, factor VII deficiency.
Factor VIII
Factor VIII deficiency prolongs the activated partial thromboplastin time and leaves the prothrombin time normal.
Factor IX
Factor IX deficiency, hemophilia B, prolongs the activated partial thromboplastin time with a normal prothrombin time.
Factor XI
Factor XI deficiency prolongs the activated partial thromboplastin time and spares the prothrombin time.

set2.io: Define: hemostasis, primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, thrombus, fibrinolysis, fibrin degradation products, D-dimer
set2.q: A 40-year-old man has a D-dimer reported. Which three enzymes act to form this cross-linked fibrin degradation product?
opts: Thrombin, factor XIII and plasmin
Correct. D-dimer results from the action of thrombin (forming fibrin), activated factor XIII (cross-linking it) and plasmin (degrading it).
Thrombin, tissue factor and factor VII
Tissue factor and factor VII start the extrinsic pathway. They help generate thrombin, but they do not degrade cross-linked fibrin into D-dimer.
Plasmin, antithrombin and protein C
Antithrombin and protein C are anticoagulant proteins that restrain clotting. D-dimer requires thrombin, factor XIII and plasmin.
Factor Xa, factor IXa and factor VIIIa
These are coagulation factors in the generation of thrombin. None of them cross-links or degrades fibrin to make D-dimer.

set2.io: Discuss diagnostic testing for: primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, fibrinolysis
set2.q: A laboratory runs a prothrombin time on a 49-year-old woman. What is added to her plasma to start the clot?
opts: A phospholipid activator
A phospholipid activator is added in the activated partial thromboplastin time to start the intrinsic pathway.
Tissue factor
Correct. The prothrombin time is the time for a fibrin clot to form in a lab tube when tissue factor is added to the patient's plasma.
Plasmin
Plasmin degrades fibrin and would dissolve a clot. It is not used to start one.
Collagen
Collagen is used to provoke platelet aggregation in function testing, not the coagulation-based prothrombin time.

set2.io: Compare and contrast laboratory studies used to evaluate bleeding and thrombotic disorders
set2.q: A 50-year-old man is evaluated for a suspected coagulation disorder. Which test is NOT among the initial screening tests?
opts: Fibrinogen level
Fibrinogen level is one of the five initial screening tests.
Activated partial thromboplastin time
The activated partial thromboplastin time is one of the initial screening tests.
Prothrombin time
The prothrombin time is one of the five initial screening tests, so it is not the exception.
D-dimer
Correct. The initial screens are the platelet count, size and shape, bleeding time, partial thromboplastin time, prothrombin time and fibrinogen level; D-dimer belongs to the thrombotic workup.

set2.io: Define: hemostasis, primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, thrombus, fibrinolysis, fibrin degradation products, D-dimer
set2.q: A 66-year-old man has a clot that formed inside his femoral vein and partly blocks flow. Which term names a clot formed in situ within the vascular system?
opts: Platelet plug
A platelet plug is what primary hemostasis forms at a site of vascular injury to arrest bleeding. A thrombus instead forms within the vessel and impedes flow.
Fibrin degradation product
Fibrin degradation products are fragments released after plasmin degrades fibrinogen or fibrin. They are what remains after a clot breaks down, not the clot itself.
D-dimer
D-dimer is a cross-linked fibrin degradation product produced when plasmin lyses a fibrin clot. It is a fragment of a clot, not the clot.
Thrombus
Correct. A thrombus is a blood clot formed in situ within the vascular system of the body that impedes blood flow.

set2.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set2.q: A 52-year-old man has a prolonged partial thromboplastin time and a normal platelet count. Which phase of hemostasis is most likely affected?
opts: Primary hemostasis
Primary hemostasis is the platelet plug, evaluated by the count, smear and function tests. A prolonged partial thromboplastin time does not test it.
Fibrinolysis
Fibrinolysis is evaluated by breakdown-product tests such as D-dimer, not by the partial thromboplastin time.
Secondary hemostasis
Correct. The partial thromboplastin time tests the intrinsic and common coagulation pathways, so a prolonged result points to the clotting factors, secondary hemostasis.
Vasoconstriction
Vasoconstriction is not measured by a clotting time. A prolonged partial thromboplastin time reflects clotting factors.

set2.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set2.q: A 67-year-old man has a prolonged prothrombin time, with a normal partial thromboplastin time, fibrinogen, D-dimer and platelet count. Which cause fits?
opts: Hemophilia A
Hemophilia A prolongs the partial thromboplastin time and leaves the prothrombin time normal.
Acute thrombosis
Acute thrombosis raises D-dimer, and the prothrombin time stays normal.
Immune thrombocytopenia
Immune thrombocytopenia lowers the platelet count and leaves the prothrombin time normal.
A vitamin K antagonist
Correct. An isolated prolonged prothrombin time with everything else normal fits liver disease, a vitamin K antagonist, factor VII deficiency or an oral factor Xa inhibitor.

set2.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set2.q: A 60-year-old woman has a prolonged thrombin time. Which pair of causes prolongs it?
opts: Warfarin and vitamin K deficiency
These prolong the prothrombin time by lowering vitamin K dependent factors, and the thrombin time stays normal.
Hemophilia A and B
In hemophilia A and B the prothrombin time and thrombin time are normal and only the partial thromboplastin time rises.
Heparin and dabigatran
Correct. Heparin and dabigatran prolong the thrombin time along with the activated partial thromboplastin time.
Factor VII and factor XII deficiency
Factor VII deficiency prolongs the prothrombin time, and factor XII deficiency prolongs the partial thromboplastin time. Neither lengthens the thrombin time.

set2.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set2.q: A 50-year-old woman with sepsis is evaluated for disseminated intravascular coagulation. Which finding is decreased?
opts: Fibrin degradation products
Fibrin degradation products are elevated in this condition, because clots are being broken down.
Prothrombin time
The prothrombin time is prolonged in this condition, not decreased, because factors are consumed.
Activated partial thromboplastin time
The partial thromboplastin time is prolonged, not decreased.
Protein C, antithrombin and protein S
Correct. In disseminated intravascular coagulation the protease inhibitors, including protein C, antithrombin and protein S, are decreased.

set2.io: Discuss diagnostic testing for: primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, fibrinolysis
set2.q: A 45-year-old woman has an isolated prolonged partial thromboplastin time that does not correct when mixed one to one with normal plasma. What does this suggest?
opts: Factor VIII deficiency
A true factor deficiency corrects because normal plasma supplies the missing factor.
An inhibitor
Correct. When a mixing study does not correct, an inhibitor is present, such as a specific factor inhibitor or lupus anticoagulant.
Factor IX deficiency
A factor IX deficiency also corrects with normal plasma, so it does not explain failure to correct.
Vitamin K deficiency
Vitamin K deficiency is a factor deficiency and would correct, and it mainly prolongs the prothrombin time.

set2.io: Describe laboratory findings associated with platelet abnormalities
set2.q: A 31-year-old man has thrombocytopenia, and his smear shows inclusions inside neutrophils. Which disorder fits?
opts: Gray platelet syndrome
Gray platelet syndrome features large, pale gray platelets rather than neutrophil inclusions.
May-Hegglin anomaly
Correct. Neutrophil inclusions on the smear point to May-Hegglin anomaly, a myosin heavy chain 9 disorder, among the morphologic causes of platelet abnormality.
Immune thrombocytopenia
Immune thrombocytopenia has a low count but no characteristic neutrophil inclusions.
Hemophilia B
Hemophilia B is a factor IX deficiency with a prolonged partial thromboplastin time and normal platelet morphology.

set2.io: Describe laboratory findings associated with platelet abnormalities
set2.q: A 41-year-old woman bleeds easily. Her platelet count, prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time are normal, and platelet function testing is abnormal. Which history best explains this?
opts: A diet very low in vitamin K
Vitamin K deficiency prolongs the prothrombin time, which is normal here.
A family history of hemophilia
Hemophilia prolongs the partial thromboplastin time and leaves platelet function normal.
Regular aspirin or nonsteroidal drug use

Correct. Aspirin and other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs give a normal count, prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time with abnormal platelet function, and patients may not realize an over-the-counter product contains them.
Long-term heparin therapy
Heparin prolongs the partial thromboplastin time and thrombin time, and it does not explain normal clotting times.

set2.io: Discuss diagnostic testing for: primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, fibrinolysis
set2.q: A 26-year-old woman has a bedside bleeding time after a standardized forearm puncture. What is being timed?
opts: How long plasma takes to clot with tissue factor
That describes the prothrombin time, a laboratory test of the extrinsic pathway on plasma in a tube.
How long the puncture keeps bleeding
Correct. Bleeding time is the time in minutes for a standardized, superficial skin puncture to stop bleeding, and it is performed at the bedside.
How long plasma takes to clot with a phospholipid activator
That describes the activated partial thromboplastin time, which assesses the intrinsic pathway in a laboratory tube.
How long a formed clot takes to dissolve
Clot dissolution is fibrinolysis, studied by tests such as D-dimer. Bleeding time measures how long a skin puncture bleeds.

set2.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set2.q: A 34-year-old woman bleeds easily. Her platelet count, prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time are all normal. Which should be investigated next?
opts: Platelet function
Correct. Normal prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time with bleeding suggest platelet dysfunction, so platelet function testing and von Willebrand studies come next.
Intrinsic pathway factors
The partial thromboplastin time is normal, which argues against an intrinsic pathway deficiency.
Extrinsic pathway factors
The prothrombin time is normal, which argues against an extrinsic pathway deficiency.
Common pathway factors
A common pathway deficiency would prolong the prothrombin time, the partial thromboplastin time or both, and both are normal here.

set2.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
set2.q: A 31-year-old man with joint bleeding has a normal prothrombin time and an activated partial thromboplastin time of 62 seconds (reference 21 to 35). Which deficiency fits?
opts: Factor VII
Factor VII deficiency prolongs the prothrombin time and leaves the activated partial thromboplastin time normal.
Factor XIII
Factor XIII deficiency leaves both the prothrombin time and the activated partial thromboplastin time normal.
Factor VIII
Correct. A prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time with a normal prothrombin time points to the intrinsic pathway; factor VIII deficiency is hemophilia A.
Fibrinogen
Low fibrinogen prolongs both the prothrombin time and the activated partial thromboplastin time.

set2.io: Define: hemostasis, primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, thrombus, fibrinolysis, fibrin degradation products, D-dimer
set2.q: A 34-year-old man cuts his finger and a platelet plug forms at the injury within minutes. Which term names this step?
opts: Secondary hemostasis
Secondary hemostasis is the next step, forming insoluble, cross-linked fibrin from activated coagulation factors, specifically thrombin. The plug comes first.
Primary hemostasis
Correct. Primary hemostasis is the formation of a platelet plug at the site of vascular injury; von Willebrand factor and glycoprotein IIb/IIIa carry it out.
Fibrinolysis
Fibrinolysis is the enzymatic breakdown of fibrin in a clot. It comes after clot formation rather than producing the initial plug.
Thrombus formation
A thrombus is a clot formed in situ within the vascular system that impedes flow, a pathologic event, not the platelet plug that arrests bleeding from a wound.
